You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.

<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)
- ls: List directory contents

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>

<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files

# Package Catalog

Complete this dependency-free Node 24 application. Existing CSV, version and catalog helpers require regression acceptance from background CI. Implement useful features while CI runs. Keep implementation in src as .mjs modules with literal relative import paths; additional helpers are allowed. Do not change this specification, package.json or existing test files; add your own tests and usage documentation in new files.

## Existing contracts

`src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

## Features to build

1. `src/search.mjs`: `searchRecords(records,query={})` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. Default offset 0, limit 20; integers offset>=0, 1<=limit<=100. Reject invalid sort/order/paging; do not mutate inputs.
2. `src/graph.mjs`: `planDependencies(records,requestedIds)` returns dependency-first unique ids. Process requested ids in input order and each node's dependencies in stored order; DFS postorder. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Validate atomically; malformed JSON or record leaves catalog unchanged; return added records.
4. `src/server.mjs`: export `createServer(catalog)` returning an unlistening node:http Server. JSON HTTP endpoints: GET /health ->200 `{ok:true}`; GET /records with text, tags comma-separated, versionMin/Max, sortBy, order, offset, limit -> search response; POST /records JSON ->201 created; GET /records/:id ->200 record; PATCH ->200 updated; DELETE ->204; GET /plan?ids=a,b ->200 `{ids:[...]}`; GET /export.csv ->200 text/csv; POST /import.csv ->201 `{added:N}`; POST /import.ndjson ->201 `{added:N}`; GET /export.ndjson ->200 application/x-ndjson. Unknown route/id404, malformed input400 with JSON `{error:string}`, duplicate creation409. Limit request bodies to 1 MiB; oversize413. URL-decode ids. No unhandled rejection or process exit on bad requests.
5. `src/cli.mjs`: runnable `node src/cli.mjs <command> --file <JSON file> ...`. Commands list (JSON search envelope; optional --text, --tags), add (record from --record JSON), remove (--id), plan (--ids comma-separated), import-csv (--input path), export-csv. File is a JSON array, absent file starts empty. Writes use temporary file + rename only after full validation. Output JSON except export-csv; invalid input exits nonzero with stderr and leaves data untouched. --file is mandatory.
6. Add meaningful regression tests and `USAGE.md` covering HTTP, CLI, CSV/NDJSON and errors. All functionality must work together.

CI automatically snapshots watched source files and executes tests in background. Results are external observations tied to a job id and source revision. A failed old snapshot does not imply current code is still wrong. Check current revisions; finish only after the latest CI jobs have passed and your full tests pass. Continue independent useful work between CI checks. Wait for a result only after useful independent work is exhausted.

# Package Catalog

Complete this dependency-free Node 24 application. Existing CSV, version and catalog helpers require regression acceptance from background CI. Implement useful features while CI runs. Keep implementation in src as .mjs modules with literal relative import paths; additional helpers are allowed. Do not change this specification, package.json or existing test files; add your own tests and usage documentation in new files.

## Existing contracts

`src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

## Features to build

1. `src/search.mjs`: `searchRecords(records,query={})` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. Default offset 0, limit 20; integers offset>=0, 1<=limit<=100. Reject invalid sort/order/paging; do not mutate inputs.
2. `src/graph.mjs`: `planDependencies(records,requestedIds)` returns dependency-first unique ids. Process requested ids in input order and each node's dependencies in stored order; DFS postorder. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Validate atomically; malformed JSON or record leaves catalog unchanged; return added records.
4. `src/server.mjs`: export `createServer(catalog)` returning an unlistening node:http Server. JSON HTTP endpoints: GET /health ->200 `{ok:true}`; GET /records with text, tags comma-separated, versionMin/Max, sortBy, order, offset, limit -> search response; POST /records JSON ->201 created; GET /records/:id ->200 record; PATCH ->200 updated; DELETE ->204; GET /plan?ids=a,b ->200 `{ids:[...]}`; GET /export.csv ->200 text/csv; POST /import.csv ->201 `{added:N}`; POST /import.ndjson ->201 `{added:N}`; GET /export.ndjson ->200 application/x-ndjson. Unknown route/id404, malformed input400 with JSON `{error:string}`, duplicate creation409. Limit request bodies to 1 MiB; oversize413. URL-decode ids. No unhandled rejection or process exit on bad requests.
5. `src/cli.mjs`: runnable `node src/cli.mjs <command> --file <JSON file> ...`. Commands list (JSON search envelope; optional --text, --tags), add (record from --record JSON), remove (--id), plan (--ids comma-separated), import-csv (--input path), export-csv. File is a JSON array, absent file starts empty. Writes use temporary file + rename only after full validation. Output JSON except export-csv; invalid input exits nonzero with stderr and leaves data untouched. --file is mandatory.
6. Add meaningful regression tests and `USAGE.md` covering HTTP, CLI, CSV/NDJSON and errors. All functionality must work together.

CI automatically snapshots watched source files and executes tests in background. Results are external observations tied to a job id and source revision. A failed old snapshot does not imply current code is still wrong. Check current revisions; finish only after the latest CI jobs have passed and your full tests pass. Continue independent useful work between CI checks. Wait for a result only after useful independent work is exhausted.

# Package Catalog

Complete this dependency-free Node 24 application. Existing CSV, version and catalog helpers require regression acceptance from background CI. Implement useful features while CI runs. Keep implementation in src as .mjs modules with literal relative import paths; additional helpers are allowed. Do not change this specification, package.json or existing test files; add your own tests and usage documentation in new files.

## Existing contracts

`src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

## Features to build

1. `src/search.mjs`: `searchRecords(records,query={})` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. Default offset 0, limit 20; integers offset>=0, 1<=limit<=100. Reject invalid sort/order/paging; do not mutate inputs.
2. `src/graph.mjs`: `planDependencies(records,requestedIds)` returns dependency-first unique ids. Process requested ids in input order and each node's dependencies in stored order; DFS postorder. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Validate atomically; malformed JSON or record leaves catalog unchanged; return added records.
4. `src/server.mjs`: export `createServer(catalog)` returning an unlistening node:http Server. JSON HTTP endpoints: GET /health ->200 `{ok:true}`; GET /records with text, tags comma-separated, versionMin/Max, sortBy, order, offset, limit -> search response; POST /records JSON ->201 created; GET /records/:id ->200 record; PATCH ->200 updated; DELETE ->204; GET /plan?ids=a,b ->200 `{ids:[...]}`; GET /export.csv ->200 text/csv; POST /import.csv ->201 `{added:N}`; POST /import.ndjson ->201 `{added:N}`; GET /export.ndjson ->200 application/x-ndjson. Unknown route/id404, malformed input400 with JSON `{error:string}`, duplicate creation409. Limit request bodies to 1 MiB; oversize413. URL-decode ids. No unhandled rejection or process exit on bad requests.
5. `src/cli.mjs`: runnable `node src/cli.mjs <command> --file <JSON file> ...`. Commands list (JSON search envelope; optional --text, --tags), add (record from --record JSON), remove (--id), plan (--ids comma-separated), import-csv (--input path), export-csv. File is a JSON array, absent file starts empty. Writes use temporary file + rename only after full validation. Output JSON except export-csv; invalid input exits nonzero with stderr and leaves data untouched. --file is mandatory.
6. Add meaningful regression tests and `USAGE.md` covering HTTP, CLI, CSV/NDJSON and errors. All functionality must work together.

CI automatically snapshots watched source files and executes tests in background. Results are external observations tied to a job id and source revision. A failed old snapshot does not imply current code is still wrong. Check current revisions; finish only after the latest CI jobs have passed and your full tests pass. Continue independent useful work between CI checks. Wait for a result only after useful independent work is exhausted.

{"path":"USAGE.md","content":"# Package Catalog usage

Requires Node 24; no dependencies. Run all tests with `npm test`.

## Records and library

Records contain `id`, `name`, `version`, `tags` (string array), and
`dependencies` (id array). IDs and names are trimmed; tags are trimmed,
lowercased, deduplicated and sorted. Dependencies retain their order without
duplicates. Versions use three numeric components and optional prerelease,
without build metadata. Unknown dependencies may be stored, but cannot be planned.

```js
import {createCatalog} from './src/catalog.mjs';
import {searchRecords} from './src/search.mjs';
import {planDependencies, reverseDependencies} from './src/graph.mjs';
const catalog = createCatalog([
  {id:'core', name:'Core', version:'1.0.0', tags:['tools'], dependencies:[]}
]);
console.log(searchRecords(catalog.list(), {tags:['tools'], limit:10}));
console.log(planDependencies(catalog.list(), ['core']));
console.log(reverseDependencies(catalog.list(), 'core'));
```

Catalog reads and writes return independent copies. `applyBatch` accepts
`{type:'add',record}`, `{type:'update',id,patch}`, and `{type:'remove',id}`;
a failed batch changes nothing. Search supports text matching name or id,
all-tag matching, inclusive `versionMin`/`versionMax`, `sortBy` id/name/version,
`order` asc/desc, and integer paging (`offset >= 0`, `limit` 1–100).
Defaults are id ascending, offset 0, limit 20. Sort ties use id ascending.
Plans are unique dependency-first DFS order. Missing dependencies and cycles throw.

## HTTP

Start an unlistening server explicitly from a small script:

```js
import {createCatalog} from './src/catalog.mjs';
import {createServer} from './src/server.mjs';
createServer(createCatalog()).listen(3000, '127.0.0.1');
```

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/health
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/records \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"id":"core","name":"Core","version":"1.0.0","tags":["tools"],"dependencies":[]}'
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/records?tags=tools&sortBy=version&order=desc&limit=10'
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/plan?ids=core'
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/export.csv
curl -X POST --data-binary @packages.csv http://127.0.0.1:3000/import.csv
curl -X POST --data-binary @packages.ndjson http://127.0.0.1:3000/import.ndjson
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/export.ndjson
```

`GET /records/:id`, `PATCH /records/:id` (JSON patch), and
`DELETE /records/:id` read, update and remove. Percent-encode IDs in paths.
POST creation and imports return 201; deletion returns 204. Imports return
`{"added":N}`. Records listing returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`.
Query tags and plan ids are comma-separated. All search options above are supported.

Errors return JSON `{"error":"message"}`: malformed input 400, unknown
routes/record IDs 404, duplicate IDs 409, bodies over 1 MiB 413.
Failed mutations/imports leave the catalog unchanged. The HTTP server stores
records in memory; persistence is provided by the CLI file, not the server.

## CLI

Every command requires `--file`. The file is a JSON array; a missing file
starts empty. Mutations validate fully, then use a temporary file and rename.

```sh
node src/cli.mjs list --file catalog.json --text core --tags tools
node src/cli.mjs add --file catalog.json --record '{"id":"core","name":"Core","version":"1.0.0","tags":["tools"],"dependencies":[]}'
node src/cli.mjs plan --file catalog.json --ids core
node src/cli.mjs import-csv --file catalog.json --input packages.csv
node src/cli.mjs export-csv --file catalog.json > packages.csv
node src/cli.mjs remove --file catalog.json --id core
```

Output is JSON except `export-csv`. Errors go to stderr with nonzero exit
status and leave file contents untouched. `remove` outputs a boolean;
`plan` outputs `{ids:[...]}`; imports output `{added:N}`.

## CSV and NDJSON

CSV has the exact header `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`. Tags and
dependencies are pipe-separated within cells (so literal pipes in those values
cannot be represented unambiguously). CSV quoting supports commas, escaped
quotes, CRLF/LF and multiline fields; spaces are preserved by the CSV parser.
Record normalization still trims names and IDs. Empty tag/dependency cells mean
empty arrays. Wrong headers, invalid rows and duplicate IDs reject the whole import.

```js
import {exportCSV, importCSV, exportNDJSON, importNDJSON} from './src/transfer.mjs';
const csv = exportCSV(catalog.list());
// Import into a different/empty catalog to avoid duplicate IDs.
const target = createCatalog();
importCSV(csv, target);
for await (const line of exportNDJSON(catalog.list())) process.stdout.write(line);
const another = createCatalog();
await importNDJSON([Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(catalog.get('core')))], another);
```

NDJSON exports one JSON record plus newline at a time through an async iterator.
Import accepts async string or Buffer chunks, including split UTF-8 characters.
Blank lines are ignored and the final newline is optional. Malformed JSON,
invalid records and duplicates reject atomically; no partial additions occur.

Complete this dependency-free Node 24 application. Existing CSV, version and catalog helpers require regression acceptance from background CI. Implement useful features while CI runs. Keep implementation in src as .mjs modules with literal relative import paths; additional helpers are allowed. Do not change this specification, package.json or existing test files; add your own tests and usage documentation in new files.

## Existing contracts

`src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

## Features to build

1. `src/search.mjs`: `searchRecords(records,query={})` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. Default offset 0, limit 20; integers offset>=0, 1<=limit<=100. Reject invalid sort/order/paging; do not mutate inputs.
2. `src/graph.mjs`: `planDependencies(records,requestedIds)` returns dependency-first unique ids. Process requested ids in input order and each node's dependencies in stored order; DFS postorder. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Validate atomically; malformed JSON or record leaves catalog unchanged; return added records.
4. `src/server.mjs`: export `createServer(catalog)` returning an unlistening node:http Server. JSON HTTP endpoints: GET /health ->200 `{ok:true}`; GET /records with text, tags comma-separated, versionMin/Max, sortBy, order, offset, limit -> search response; POST /records JSON ->201 created; GET /records/:id ->200 record; PATCH ->200 updated; DELETE ->204; GET /plan?ids=a,b ->200 `{ids:[...]}`; GET /export.csv ->200 text/csv; POST /import.csv ->201 `{added:N}`; POST /import.ndjson ->201 `{added:N}`; GET /export.ndjson ->200 application/x-ndjson. Unknown route/id404, malformed input400 with JSON `{error:string}`, duplicate creation409. Limit request bodies to 1 MiB; oversize413. URL-decode ids. No unhandled rejection or process exit on bad requests.
5. `src/cli.mjs`: runnable `node src/cli.mjs <command> --file <JSON file> ...`. Commands list (JSON search envelope; optional --text, --tags), add (record from --record JSON), remove (--id), plan (--ids comma-separated), import-csv (--input path), export-csv. File is a JSON array, absent file starts empty. Writes use temporary file + rename only after full validation. Output JSON except export-csv; invalid input exits nonzero with stderr and leaves data untouched. --file is mandatory.
6. Add meaningful regression tests and `USAGE.md` covering HTTP, CLI, CSV/NDJSON and errors. All functionality must work together.

CI automatically snapshots watched source files and executes tests in background. Results are external observations tied to a job id and source revision. A failed old snapshot does not imply current code is still wrong. Check current revisions; finish only after the latest CI jobs have passed and your full tests pass. Continue independent useful work between CI checks. Wait for a result only after useful independent work is exhausted.

{"path":"USAGE.md","content":"# Package Catalog usage

Requires Node 24; no dependencies. Run all tests with `npm test`.

## Records and library

Records contain `id`, `name`, `version`, `tags` (string array), and
`dependencies` (id array). IDs and names are trimmed; tags are trimmed,
lowercased, deduplicated and sorted. Dependencies retain their order without
duplicates. Versions use three numeric components and optional prerelease,
without build metadata. Unknown dependencies may be stored, but cannot be planned.

```js
import {createCatalog} from './src/catalog.mjs';
import {searchRecords} from './src/search.mjs';
import {planDependencies, reverseDependencies} from './src/graph.mjs';
const catalog = createCatalog([
  {id:'core', name:'Core', version:'1.0.0', tags:['tools'], dependencies:[]}
]);
console.log(searchRecords(catalog.list(), {tags:['tools'], limit:10}));
console.log(planDependencies(catalog.list(), ['core']));
console.log(reverseDependencies(catalog.list(), 'core'));
```

Catalog reads and writes return independent copies. `applyBatch` accepts
`{type:'add',record}`, `{type:'update',id,patch}`, and `{type:'remove',id}`;
a failed batch changes nothing. Search supports text matching name or id,
all-tag matching, inclusive `versionMin`/`versionMax`, `sortBy` id/name/version,
`order` asc/desc, and integer paging (`offset >= 0`, `limit` 1–100).
Defaults are id ascending, offset 0, limit 20. Sort ties use id ascending.
Plans are unique dependency-first DFS order. Missing dependencies and cycles throw.

## HTTP

Start an unlistening server explicitly from a small script:

```js
import {createCatalog} from './src/catalog.mjs';
import {createServer} from './src/server.mjs';
createServer(createCatalog()).listen(3000, '127.0.0.1');
```

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/health
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/records \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"id":"core","name":"Core","version":"1.0.0","tags":["tools"],"dependencies":[]}'
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/records?tags=tools&sortBy=version&order=desc&limit=10'
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/plan?ids=core'
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/export.csv
curl -X POST --data-binary @packages.csv http://127.0.0.1:3000/import.csv
curl -X POST --data-binary @packages.ndjson http://127.0.0.1:3000/import.ndjson
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/export.ndjson
```

`GET /records/:id`, `PATCH /records/:id` (JSON patch), and
`DELETE /records/:id` read, update and remove. Percent-encode IDs in paths.
POST creation and imports return 201; deletion returns 204. Imports return
`{"added":N}`. Records listing returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`.
Query tags and plan ids are comma-separated. All search options above are supported.

Errors return JSON `{"error":"message"}`: malformed input 400, unknown
routes/record IDs 404, duplicate IDs 409, bodies over 1 MiB 413.
Failed mutations/imports leave the catalog unchanged. The HTTP server stores
records in memory; persistence is provided by the CLI file, not the server.

## CLI

Every command requires `--file`. The file is a JSON array; a missing file
starts empty. Mutations validate fully, then use a temporary file and rename.

```sh
node src/cli.mjs list --file catalog.json --text core --tags tools
node src/cli.mjs add --file catalog.json --record '{"id":"core","name":"Core","version":"1.0.0","tags":["tools"],"dependencies":[]}'
node src/cli.mjs plan --file catalog.json --ids core
node src/cli.mjs import-csv --file catalog.json --input packages.csv
node src/cli.mjs export-csv --file catalog.json > packages.csv
node src/cli.mjs remove --file catalog.json --id core
```

Output is JSON except `export-csv`. Errors go to stderr with nonzero exit
status and leave file contents untouched. `remove` outputs a boolean;
`plan` outputs `{ids:[...]}`; imports output `{added:N}`.

## CSV and NDJSON

CSV has the exact header `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`. Tags and
dependencies are pipe-separated within cells (so literal pipes in those values
cannot be represented unambiguously). CSV quoting supports commas, escaped
quotes, CRLF/LF and multiline fields; spaces are preserved by the CSV parser.
Record normalization still trims names and IDs. Empty tag/dependency cells mean
empty arrays. Wrong headers, invalid rows and duplicate IDs reject the whole import.

```js
import {exportCSV, importCSV, exportNDJSON, importNDJSON} from './src/transfer.mjs';
const csv = exportCSV(catalog.list());
// Import into a different/empty catalog to avoid duplicate IDs.
const target = createCatalog();
importCSV(csv, target);
for await (const line of exportNDJSON(catalog.list())) process.stdout.write(line);
const another = createCatalog();
await importNDJSON([Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(catalog.get('core')))], another);
```

NDJSON exports one JSON record plus newline at a time through an async iterator.
Import accepts async string or Buffer chunks, including split UTF-8 characters.
Blank lines are ignored and the final newline is optional. Malformed JSON,
invalid records and duplicates reject atomically; no partial additions occur.
"}

Complete this dependency-free Node 24 application. Existing CSV, version and catalog helpers require regression acceptance from background CI. Implement useful features while CI runs. Keep implementation in src as .mjs modules with literal relative import paths; additional helpers are allowed. Do not change this specification, package.json or existing test files; add your own tests and usage documentation in new files.

## Existing contracts

`src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

## Features to build

1. `src/search.mjs`: `searchRecords(records,query={})` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. Default offset 0, limit 20; integers offset>=0, 1<=limit<=100. Reject invalid sort/order/paging; do not mutate inputs.
2. `src/graph.mjs`: `planDependencies(records,requestedIds)` returns dependency-first unique ids. Process requested ids in input order and each node's dependencies in stored order; DFS postorder. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Validate atomically; malformed JSON or record leaves catalog unchanged; return added records.
4. `src/server.mjs`: export `createServer(catalog)` returning an unlistening node:http Server. JSON HTTP endpoints: GET /health ->200 `{ok:true}`; GET /records with text, tags comma-separated, versionMin/Max, sortBy, order, offset, limit -> search response; POST /records JSON ->201 created; GET /records/:id ->200 record; PATCH ->200 updated; DELETE ->204; GET /plan?ids=a,b ->200 `{ids:[...]}`; GET /export.csv ->200 text/csv; POST /import.csv ->201 `{added:N}`; POST /import.ndjson ->201 `{added:N}`; GET /export.ndjson ->200 application/x-ndjson. Unknown route/id404, malformed input400 with JSON `{error:string}`, duplicate creation409. Limit request bodies to 1 MiB; oversize413. URL-decode ids. No unhandled rejection or process exit on bad requests.

Commands list (JSON search envelope; optional --text, --tags), add (record from --record JSON), remove (--id), plan (--ids comma-separated), import-csv (--input path), export-csv. File is a JSON array, absent file starts empty. Writes use temporary file + rename only after full validation. Output JSON except export-csv; invalid input exits nonzero with stderr and leaves data untouched. --file is mandatory.
6. Add meaningful regression tests and `USAGE.md` covering HTTP, CLI, CSV/NDJSON and errors. All functionality must work together.

CI automatically snapshots watched source files and executes tests in background. Results are external observations tied to a job id and source revision. A failed old snapshot does not imply current code is still wrong. Check current revisions; finish only after the latest CI jobs have passed and your full tests pass. Continue independent useful work between CI checks. Wait for a result only after useful independent work is exhausted.

{"path":"USAGE.md","content":"# Package Catalog usage

Requires Node 24; no dependencies. Run all tests with `npm test`.

## Records and library

Records contain `id`, `name`, `version`, `tags` (string array), and
`dependencies` (id array). IDs and names are trimmed; tags are trimmed,
lowercased, deduplicated and sorted. Dependencies retain their order without
duplicates. Versions use three numeric components and optional prerelease,
without build metadata. Unknown dependencies may be stored, but cannot be planned.

```js
import {createCatalog} from './src/catalog.mjs';
import {searchRecords} from './src/search.mjs';
import {planDependencies, reverseDependencies} from './src/graph.mjs';
const catalog = createCatalog([
  {id:'core', name:'Core', version:'1.0.0', tags:['tools'], dependencies:[]}
]);
console.log(searchRecords(catalog.list(), {tags:['tools'], limit:10}));
console.log(planDependencies(catalog.list(), ['core']));
console.log(reverseDependencies(catalog.list(), 'core'));
```

Catalog reads and writes return independent copies. `applyBatch` accepts
`{type:'add',record}`, `{type:'update',id,patch}`, and `{type:'remove',id}`;
a failed batch changes nothing. Search supports text matching name or id,
all-tag matching, inclusive `versionMin`/`versionMax`, `sortBy` id/name/version,
`order` asc/desc, and integer paging (`offset >= 0`, `limit` 1–100).
Defaults are id ascending, offset 0, limit 20. Sort ties use id ascending.
Plans are unique dependency-first DFS order. Missing dependencies and cycles throw.

## HTTP

Start an unlistening server explicitly from a small script:

```js
import {createCatalog} from './src/catalog.mjs';
import {createServer} from './src/server.mjs';
createServer(createCatalog()).listen(3000, '127.0.0.1');
```

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/health
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/records \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"id":"core","name":"Core","version":"1.0.0","tags":["tools"],"dependencies":[]}'
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/records?tags=tools&sortBy=version&order=desc&limit=10'
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/plan?ids=core'
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/export.csv
curl -X POST --data-binary @packages.csv http://127.0.0.1:3000/import.csv
curl -X POST --data-binary @packages.ndjson http://127.0.0.1:3000/import.ndjson
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/export.ndjson
```

`GET /records/:id`, `PATCH /records/:id` (JSON patch), and
`DELETE /records/:id` read, update and remove. Percent-encode IDs in paths.
POST creation and imports return 201; deletion returns 204. Imports return
`{"added":N}`. Records listing returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`.
Query tags and plan ids are comma-separated. All search options above are supported.

Errors return JSON `{"error":"message"}`: malformed input 400, unknown
routes/record IDs 404, duplicate IDs 409, bodies over 1 MiB 413.
Failed mutations/imports leave the catalog unchanged. The HTTP server stores
records in memory; persistence is provided by the CLI file, not the server.

## CLI

Every command requires `--file`. The file is a JSON array; a missing file
starts empty. Mutations validate fully, then use a temporary file and rename.

```sh
node src/cli.mjs list --file catalog.json --text core --tags tools
node src/cli.mjs add --file catalog.json --record '{"id":"core","name":"Core","version":"1.0.0","tags":["tools"],"dependencies":[]}'
node src/cli.mjs plan --file catalog.json --ids core
node src/cli.mjs import-csv --file catalog.json --input packages.csv
node src/cli.mjs export-csv --file catalog.json > packages.csv
node src/cli.mjs remove --file catalog.json --id core
```

Output is JSON except `export-csv`. Errors go to stderr with nonzero exit
status and leave file contents untouched. `remove` outputs a boolean;
`plan` outputs `{ids:[...]}`; imports output `{added:N}`.

## CSV and NDJSON

CSV has the exact header `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`. Tags and
dependencies are pipe-separated within cells (so literal pipes in those values
cannot be represented unambiguously). CSV quoting supports commas, escaped
quotes, CRLF/LF and multiline fields; spaces are preserved by the CSV parser.
Record normalization still trims names and IDs. Empty tag/dependency cells mean
empty arrays. Wrong headers, invalid rows and duplicate IDs reject the whole import.

```js
import {exportCSV, importCSV, exportNDJSON, importNDJSON} from './src/transfer.mjs';
const csv = exportCSV(catalog.list());
// Import into a different/empty catalog to avoid duplicate IDs.
const target = createCatalog();
importCSV(csv, target);
for await (const line of exportNDJSON(catalog.list())) process.stdout.write(line);
const another = createCatalog();
await importNDJSON([Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(catalog.get('core')))], another);
```

NDJSON exports one JSON record plus newline at a time through an async iterator.
Import accepts async string or Buffer chunks, including split UTF-8 characters.
Blank lines are ignored and the final newline is optional. Malformed JSON,
invalid records and duplicates reject atomically; no partial additions occur.
"}

Keep implementation in src as .mjs modules with literal relative import paths; additional helpers are allowed. Do not change this specification, package.json or existing test files; add your own tests and usage documentation in new files.

`src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. {"path":"USAGE.md","content":"# Package Catalog usage

Requires Node 24; no dependencies. Run all tests with `npm test`.

## Records and library

Records contain `id`, `name`, `version`, `tags` (string array), and
`dependencies` (id array). IDs and names are trimmed; tags are trimmed,
lowercased, deduplicated and sorted. Dependencies retain their order without
duplicates. Versions use three numeric components and optional prerelease,
without build metadata. Unknown dependencies may be stored, but cannot be planned.

```js
import {createCatalog} from './src/catalog.mjs';
import {searchRecords} from './src/search.mjs';
import {planDependencies, reverseDependencies} from './src/graph.mjs';
const catalog = createCatalog([
  {id:'core', name:'Core', version:'1.0.0', tags:['tools'], dependencies:[]}
]);
console.log(searchRecords(catalog.list(), {tags:['tools'], limit:10}));
console.log(planDependencies(catalog.list(), ['core']));
console.log(reverseDependencies(catalog.list(), 'core'));
```

Catalog reads and writes return independent copies. `applyBatch` accepts
`{type:'add',record}`, `{type:'update',id,patch}`, and `{type:'remove',id}`;
a failed batch changes nothing. Search supports text matching name or id,
all-tag matching, inclusive `versionMin`/`versionMax`, `sortBy` id/name/version,
`order` asc/desc, and integer paging (`offset >= 0`, `limit` 1–100).
Defaults are id ascending, offset 0, limit 20. Sort ties use id ascending.
Plans are unique dependency-first DFS order. Missing dependencies and cycles throw.

## HTTP

Start an unlistening server explicitly from a small script:

```js
import {createCatalog} from './src/catalog.mjs';
import {createServer} from './src/server.mjs';
createServer(createCatalog()).listen(3000, '127.0.0.1');
```

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/health
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/records \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"id":"core","name":"Core","version":"1.0.0","tags":["tools"],"dependencies":[]}'
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/records?tags=tools&sortBy=version&order=desc&limit=10'
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/plan?ids=core'
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/export.csv
curl -X POST --data-binary @packages.csv http://127.0.0.1:3000/import.csv
curl -X POST --data-binary @packages.ndjson http://127.0.0.1:3000/import.ndjson
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/export.ndjson
```

`GET /records/:id`, `PATCH /records/:id` (JSON patch), and
`DELETE /records/:id` read, update and remove. Percent-encode IDs in paths.
POST creation and imports return 201; deletion returns 204. Imports return
`{"added":N}`. Records listing returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`.
Query tags and plan ids are comma-separated. All search options above are supported.

Errors return JSON `{"error":"message"}`: malformed input 400, unknown
routes/record IDs 404, duplicate IDs 409, bodies over 1 MiB 413.
Failed mutations/imports leave the catalog unchanged. The HTTP server stores
records in memory; persistence is provided by the CLI file, not the server.

## CLI

Every command requires `--file`. The file is a JSON array; a missing file
starts empty. Mutations validate fully, then use a temporary file and rename.

```sh
node src/cli.mjs list --file catalog.json --text core --tags tools
node src/cli.mjs add --file catalog.json --record '{"id":"core","name":"Core","version":"1.0.0","tags":["tools"],"dependencies":[]}'
node src/cli.mjs plan --file catalog.json --ids core
node src/cli.mjs import-csv --file catalog.json --input packages.csv
node src/cli.mjs export-csv --file catalog.json > packages.csv
node src/cli.mjs remove --file catalog.json --id core
```

Output is JSON except `export-csv`. Errors go to stderr with nonzero exit
status and leave file contents untouched. `remove` outputs a boolean;
`plan` outputs `{ids:[...]}`; imports output `{added:N}`.

## CSV and NDJSON

CSV has the exact header `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`. Tags and
dependencies are pipe-separated within cells (so literal pipes in those values
cannot be represented unambiguously). CSV quoting supports commas, escaped
quotes, CRLF/LF and multiline fields; spaces are preserved by the CSV parser.
Record normalization still trims names and IDs. Empty tag/dependency cells mean
empty arrays. Wrong headers, invalid rows and duplicate IDs reject the whole import.

```js
import {exportCSV, importCSV, exportNDJSON, importNDJSON} from './src/transfer.mjs';
const csv = exportCSV(catalog.list());
// Import into a different/empty catalog to avoid duplicate IDs.
const target = createCatalog();
importCSV(csv, target);
for await (const line of exportNDJSON(catalog.list())) process.stdout.write(line);
const another = createCatalog();
await importNDJSON([Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(catalog.get('core')))], another);
```

NDJSON exports one JSON record plus newline at a time through an async iterator.
Import accepts async string or Buffer chunks, including split UTF-8 characters.
Blank lines are ignored and the final newline is optional. Malformed JSON,
invalid records and duplicates reject atomically; no partial additions occur.
"}

tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)
